header.question:
A document in the library contains this sentence:

> Another important tool is mechanistic analysis, i.e. studying the model's weights and activations for understanding how it functions, which has been shown to fully explain the behavior of entire neural networks (Nanda et al., 2023; Olah et al., 2020).

Check what the sentence says about the work it cites against that work in the library. Does the cited source support it? Cite the page(s) of the cited source that show what it actually says.

args.query: mechanistic analysis "studying the model's weights and activations"
Nanda Olah mechanistic interpretability fully explain behavior neural networks
Zoom In: An Introduction to Circuits
Progress measures for grokking via mechanistic interpretability

args.text:
Verdict: not supported

The sentence is a paraphrase of a passage in *Model evaluation for extreme risks* (arxiv:2305.15324/v2/p12). That passage cites Nanda et al., 2023 and Olah et al., 2020 only for a much weaker claim. It says: "studying the model’s weights and activations for understanding how it functions (Nanda et al., 2023; Olah et al., 2020)" (arxiv:2305.15324/v2/p12). It describes mechanistic analysis as a tool, with ambitions such as studying how a model's goals are represented internally and detecting when a model's outputs misreport its knowledge. It makes no claim that mechanistic analysis has "been shown to fully explain the behavior of entire neural networks." The phrase "fully explain" does not appear on any page of the library.

The cited works are not in the library as full texts. They appear only in the reference list. Nanda et al. is listed as "Progress measures for grokking via mechanistic interpretability" (arxiv:2305.15324/v2/p17), and Olah et al. as "Zoom in: An introduction to circuits" (arxiv:2305.15324/v2/p18). So I can check the citing paper's description of them, but not what those works themselves show. Nothing in the library supports the "fully explain" claim.
